Nah, joking. Like the other guy said, switching OS won't help your drives to not fail mechanically. I would recommend rolling your own NAS with redundant storage, mirrored hard drives. If one fails, you have an exact copy on the other. Replace the failed drive, mirror the data back over to it, and your data is safe again barring some catastrophic system failure. A NAS, by the way, can be as simple as a basic computer with two hard drives in it running something like FreeNAS.

I don't recommend backing up remote, even encrypted, because you're handing over your data to a third party who you can never be certain is trustworthy. They can be coerced to release it to authorities who can then either break the encryption on their own or force you to decrypt it. Same thing is possible if for some reason your drives are seized from your home, but at least that was on your own watch.
